title: Understanding the Model
text: The model we are using is $f_theta(z)=theta*z$. Since we are given $$\$x=1\$$$, we need to find the optimal $theta$ for this scenario.

title: Optimal Theta Calculation
text: To find the optimal $theta$, consider the training data point $(x,y)$ where $$\$x=1\$$$ and $y=g(x)=A*x**2$. Substitute these into the model equation.

title: Substitute and Solve
text: Substitute $$\$x=1\$$$ and $$\$y=A 1^2=A\$$$ into the model equation $f_theta(x)=theta*x$. This gives $theta*1=A$. Solve for $theta$.

title: Bias and Variance at Test Point
text: Now that we have $$\$theta=A\$$$, evaluate the bias and variance of the model $f_theta$ at the test point $$\$z=1\$$$.

title: Bias Calculation
text: The bias is the difference between the expected prediction of the model and the true function value at $$\$z=1\$$$. Calculate $f_theta(1)$ and compare it to $g(1)$.

title: Variance Calculation
text: Since there is no noise ($sigma**2=0$), the variance of the model's prediction at $$\$z=1\$$$ is zero. Confirm this by considering the variance of $f_theta(1)$.
